items.longBusinessSummary: Equinox Gold Corp. engages in the acquisition, exploration, development, and operation of mineral properties in the Americas. It primarily explores gold and silver deposits. The company was formerly known as Trek Mining Inc. and changed its name to Equinox Gold Corp. in December 2017. Equinox Gold Corp. was incorporated in 2007 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

Title: Equinox Gold Reports Q3 Production of 237,019 Ounces, Maintains 2026 Guidance
Author: MT Newswires   October 13, 2026 1 min read
Published: 2026-10-13T11:25:22+00:00
=== BODY ===
Equinox Gold (EQX) reported Tuesday Q3 gold production of 237,019 ounces and sales of 248,484 ounces, including two months of contributions from its Orla Mining acquisition.The company said it produced 611,483 ounces year to date and maintained its updated 2026 production guidance of 870,000 to 920,000 ounces. Equinox also said it repaid $190 million in debt during the quarter ended Sept. 30 and had $527 million in cash at the end of the quarter. The company said it also began early construction work at its South Railroad project in Nevada, targeting first gold production in 2028.Equinox Gold shares were up 2% in premarket activity Tuesday.

Title: Barrick Sinks 5.7% as Freedom Broker Cuts Gold Majors to Hold, Slashes Target to $46
Author: Gian Estrada   Thu, October 22, 2026 at 7:04 PM GMT+2 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-22T17:04:27+00:00
=== BODY ===
Barrick shares fell 5.7% today after Freedom Broker cut the stock to Hold from Buy and lowered its price target to $46 from $54.
Freedom Broker also downgraded Newmont and Agnico Eagle. AngloGold Ashanti and Equinox Gold fell even more than Barrick without a downgrade, which points to gold's slide as a major driver.
Analysts still expect Barrick's normalized EPS to rise from $2.42 in fiscal 2025 to $4.22 in fiscal 2027.
Barrick's forward P/E is well below its five-year average, and its third-quarter report on Nov. 9 is the next test.
Barrick Mining (B) shares sank 5.7% today after Freedom Broker cut the gold miner to Hold from Buy and lowered its price target to $46 from $54.
Freedom Broker analyst Vitaly Kononov downgraded Newmont (NEM:NYSE) and Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM:NYSE) to Hold at the same time, and those stocks fell 4.5% and 6.4%. But AngloGold Ashanti (AU:NYSE) dropped 6.1% and Equinox Gold (EQX) 6% without a downgrade from Freedom Broker.
Freedom Broker did trim its Barrick estimates, but it still credits the miner with an "attractive earnings trajectory."
Look at AngloGold and Equinox. Freedom Broker didn't downgrade either one, and both fell harder than Barrick during the broader selloff. Kinross Gold (KGC) fell nearly as much without a downgrade. Newmont, one of the three stocks Freedom Broker cut, fell the least of the group.
What these stocks have in common is gold. Spot gold fell about 2% today to around $4,050 an ounce, its lowest level since early August and well below January's record near $5,600. Miners tend to magnify the metal's moves. The S&P 500 was also down about 1%, so the whole group took the hit.
See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Barrick Mining, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Barrick Mining's Analyst Ratings
Analysts as a group still expect Barrick's normalized EPS to rise from $2.42 in fiscal 2025 to $3.56 this year and $4.22 in 2027.
The stock wasn't priced for perfection going in, either. At Wednesday's close, Barrick traded at 11x forward earnings, well under its five-year average of nearly 15x.
The pattern across the group suggests gold's decline contributed to Barrick's selloff alongside the downgrade. The broker trimmed its estimates, but the Street as a whole still expects Barrick's earnings to keep climbing, and the stock now costs less for that growth. Freedom Broker's new $46 target sits below the Street's $51 consensus, and it's still well above where the stock trades today.
If gold keeps sliding, those EPS estimates will follow it down.
Newmont reports its third quarter after today's close, and Agnico Eagle reports next week. That gives investors a read on the group before Barrick reports before the open on Monday, Nov. 9.

Title: 3 Reasons Why Growth Investors Shouldn't Overlook Equinox Gold (EQX)
Author: Zacks Equity Research   October 14, 2026 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-14T15:45:02+00:00
=== BODY ===
Investors seek growth stocks to capitalize on above-average growth in financials that help these securities grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. But finding a growth stock that can live up to its true potential can be a tough task.
In addition to volatility, these stocks carry above-average risk by their very nature. Also, one could end up losing from a stock whose growth story is actually over or nearing its end.
However, the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects, makes it pretty easy to find cutting-edge growth stocks.
Our proprietary system currently recommends Equinox Gold (EQX) as one such stock. This company not only has a favorable Growth Score, but also carries a top Zacks Rank.
Research shows that stocks carrying the best growth features consistently beat the market. And returns are even better for stocks that possess the combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy).
While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this gold miner is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:
Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. For growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is highly preferable, as it is often perceived as an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.
While the historical EPS growth rate for Equinox Gold is 230.8%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 259.2% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 39.1%.
While cash is the lifeblood of any business, higher-than-average cash flow growth is more important and beneficial for growth-oriented companies than for mature companies. That's because, growth in cash flow enables these companies to expand their businesses without depending on expensive outside funds.
Right now, year-over-year cash flow growth for Equinox Gold is 79.5%, which is higher than many of its peers. In fact, the rate compares to the industry average of 42.8%.
While investors should actually consider the current cash flow growth, it's worth taking a look at the historical rate too for putting the current reading into proper perspective. The company's annualized cash flow growth rate has been 18.4% over the past 3-5 years versus the industry average of 12.9%.
Beyond the metrics outlined above, investors should consider the trend in earnings estimate revisions. A positive trend is a plus here. Empirical research shows that there is a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.
The current-year earnings estimates for Equinox Gold have been revising upward. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has surged 0.7% over the past month.
While the overall earnings estimate revisions have made Equinox Gold a Zacks Rank #2 stock, it has earned itself a Growth Score of B based on a number of factors, including the ones discussed above.
You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.
This combination indicates that Equinox Gold is a potential outperformer and a solid choice for growth investors.
